Feature Extraction Results

This report summarises distribution and correlation patterns of extracted features across genomic regions, grouped by sample or experimental condition. The plots provide an overview of how specific features vary between samples and how they relate to one another.

Feature Extraction Summary

This report visualises the distribution and co-variation of extracted features, such as modification levels or coverage metrics, across a set of genomic regions. Features are extracted from one or more input datasets (e.g., bed files), optionally grouped by sample metadata.

Two types of visualisations are provided:

  • Violin plots showing the distribution of feature values across samples or groups
  • Correlation heatmaps showing Pearson correlation coefficients between samples based on feature values

These plots can help identify technical variability, group separation, and outliers in feature distributions.

Feature Distribution (Violin Plots)

Each violin plot displays the distribution of a particular feature (e.g., methylation fraction or count) across all samples or grouped categories. These plots allow for visual comparison of feature variability and central tendency between groups.

Sample Correlation (Heatmaps)

Correlation heatmaps display pairwise Pearson correlations between samples, computed from the extracted feature values. This helps assess technical consistency between replicates and potential group clustering based on sample similarity.
